directions: Section II, Long Essay Question (LEQ). Suggested time: 40 minutes. This question counts for 15 percent of your exam score. There is one prompt and no choices. In your response you should develop a historically defensible thesis that establishes a line of reasoning, describe a broader historical context relevant to the prompt, support your argument with at least two pieces of specific and relevant evidence, use historical reasoning to frame your argument, and demonstrate a complex understanding of a historical development related to the prompt.
inspired_by: Practice Test 4, LEQ trio - remapped to Fall 2026 CED format (single broad prompt)

evidence: The Wilmot Proviso (1846) made slavery in the Mexican Cession the central political issue, splitting both national parties along sectional lines
The Kansas-Nebraska Act (1854) repealed the Missouri Compromise line, produced Bleeding Kansas, and drove antislavery Northerners into the new Republican Party
The Dred Scott decision (1857) and the Lincoln-Douglas debates showed that the territorial question had become inseparable from the moral conflict over slavery itself
exemplar.thesis: The Mexican-American War led to the Civil War to a large extent: by adding vast new territory, it forced the slavery-expansion question into national politics, destroyed the existing party system, and produced a purely sectional Republican Party whose victory made Southern secession possible - though long-standing moral and economic conflicts over slavery gave the territorial crisis its explosive force.

items.intro: The war between the United States and Mexico (1846-1848) ended with the Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo, which transferred California and the vast Southwest to the United States. Within a few years, Americans were fighting - in Congress, in Kansas, and finally on battlefields - over whether slavery would be permitted in the new territory.
items.original_prompt: Evaluate the extent to which the Mexican-American War led to the American Civil War in the time period 1840 to 1860.
items.prompt: Evaluate the extent to which the Mexican-American War led to the American Civil War in the period 1844 to 1860.
suggested_areas: Political developments, such as the Wilmot Proviso, the Compromise of 1850, the Kansas-Nebraska Act, and the formation of the Republican Party
Economic developments, such as the expansion of plantation slavery and debates over free versus enslaved labor in the West
Social and ideological developments, such as the growth of abolitionism, Southern defenses of slavery, and the idea of popular sovereignty
